(2) Where in any. trial of an offence under section sub-section (I), if the fact that the accused-person or any other person on his behalf has acquired or is in possession of property, movable or immovable disproportionate to his known sources of income, is proved the Court shall presume, unless the accused succeeds to rebut such presumption in the Court, that the accused person is guilty of said offence and a conviction thereof shall not be invalid by reason only that it is based on such presumption." 

 9. It transpires from the FIR and charge sheet that there is independent allegation against the accused petitioner Mrs. Rowshena Jahan that she was owning and possessing some properties which are alleged to be disproportionate to her known source of income. It is necessary to spell out as to how she acquired those properties. Therefore the accused-petitioner is liable to rebut presumption in the Court during the trial as contemplated under section 27(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. 2004, quoted above. If the trial is not allowed it would not be possible to ascertain as to whether her husband accused No.1 acquired the those properties in the name of his wife or the accused-petitioner her- self acquired the same in any other way. It is also necessary to ascertain the source of money for the acquisition of those properties.
